messages:
Maria G: Quick idea — thinking about decomposing the routing policy/eval into two cooperating adapters: an SLO-enforcer (hard constraints) and a Preference/Scoring resolver (soft weights). Goal: make runtime fail-fast on SLOs but keep rich preference logic pluggable and off the hot path. Thoughts?
Alex P: sounds promising. main q: when the SLO-enforcer says 'can't meet SLO' what should it do? fallback to degraded model? queue? reject? we need a consistent action space. :thinking:
Tyler: +1. propose a small contract: adapters receive request_context and a list of candidate routes and return ordered candidates + an explicit fallback_action enum. Example (pseudo):
```json
{
  "candidates": ["route-a","route-b"],
  "scores": [0.9,0.6],
  "fallback_action": "downgrade_model",
  "explain": "latency_budget_exceeded -> prefer lower-latency-variant"
}
```
Cheng: decomposition is clean but two concerns: extra RPCs on the hot path (latency), and more surface area for bugs. maybe co-locate SLO-enforcer in the router and have the Preference resolver be async or cached.
Samira: telemetry + rollout guard is a must. we should gate SLO-enforcer per-tenant with feature flags and canary percent. also need clear metrics: slo_enforcer.decisions, decision_latency_ms, fallback_counts, explain_size_bytes.
Maria G: agree re metrics. My rough action semantics list: ["downgrade_model","route_to_compatible_region","apply_queue_with_timeout","return_error"]. each action should include optional params, e.g. queue_timeout_ms or target_variant. propose we standardize keys: latency_budget_ms, error_budget_pct, cost_cap_usd, region_affinity.
Alex P: also require adapters to include a tiny "explain" blob (<=512 bytes) so we can surface why route chosen in logs/UI. no verbose traces in hot path.
Tyler: on the RPC cost worry: make SLO-enforcer extremely cheap — only check SLO constraints against telemetry + available capacity snapshot. Preference resolver can be heavier and run from cache or precompute per-tenant profiles. also support an optimization: SLO-enforcer can short-circuit and return "delegate_to_cached_pref" to avoid full resolver call.
Cheng: idempotency note: adapters must be side-effect free. runtime should not rely on adapter to mutate state. any mutating ops must go through a controlled async workflow.
Samira: rollout plan sketch: 1) RFC with schema + examples, 2) unit perf benchmark for SLO-enforcer (p95 budget), 3) deploy SLO-enforcer in shadow mode for 2 weeks, 4) enable 5% tenants, 5) ramp. add rollback playbook.
Maria G: propose contract proto keys (final draft):
```json
{
  "request_context": {"tenant_id":"t-123","token_count":72,"route_hint":"edge-us-west"},
  "slo_constraints": {"latency_budget_ms":150,"error_budget_pct":0.5,"cost_cap_usd":0.02},
  "adapter_response": {"ordered_routes":[{"route":"r1","score":0.83}],"fallback_action":"route_to_compatible_region","explain":"p95 local > budget"}
}
```
Alex P: also require a small numeric 'confidence' field for each candidate so the runtime can decide when to hedge or fall back. and add 'telemetry_staleness_ms' to request_context so adapters know if their inputs are stale.
Tyler: thought: support hybrid fallback policies like 'downgrade_model unless region_latency < X then route_cross_region'. We can encode as a short boolean clause in response, e.g. `conditional_fallback`: "if cross_region_latency < 250 -> route_cross_region else downgrade_model". keep it simple.
Samira: ops safety: when SLO-enforcer returns aggressive fallbacks we need automatic throttles to avoid cost runaway. tie fallback counts into cost alarms and auto-disable the pref resolver if cost_cap breached.
Cheng: performance tests we need: (A) SLO-enforcer latency microbench (cold start + hot path), (B) end-to-end per-request additional ms, (C) percent of requests that trigger fallback, (D) memory/RPC load.
Maria G: proposed owners: I'll draft RFC + schema -> @Tyler will prototype minimal adapter impl -> @Samira will own canary/telemetry gating -> @Cheng will run perf tests -> @Alex will add observability wire-ups.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout job started for slo-enforcer-prototype (10% tenants).
Alex P: one more: require adapters to return stable route ids (opaque) so analytics can join decisions to traces. avoid human-readable heuristics in ids.
Samira: action item: add safety flag 'allow_unbounded_cost': false by default and require explicit enterprise override.
Maria G: ok good discussion — I'll start the RFC and include example contract + decision matrix. thanks all :tada:
Tyler: lgtm, will start a toy impl this week.
Cheng: will schedule perf run for Friday.
Samira: I'll add monitoring playbook to the RFC.
Maria G: closing thread — leave notes in the RFC doc when done.
